residual_evaluator_ordering.stack: 625-ID residual state + cardinality bound + exact tactical/forced normalization
residual_evaluator_ordering.timing_protocol: 13 rotating-order repetitions; first 5 excluded as warm-up; medians over remaining 8
residual_evaluator_ordering.interpretation: Exponential residual requirement-maturity ordering materially improves proof order after forced normalization, but the high-level prototype still pays more elapsed time. Caching the already-built child transition reduces the earlier timing loss substantially. Node-effect confidence rises; production time-effect confidence remains unresolved pending fixed-width/incremental scoring.

allis_a1_a3.compatibility: conservative: rule instances in a selected cover must have disjoint required-square masks
allis_a1_a3.cohort: deterministic random nonterminal 7x6 roots, ply 22..32, exact decision-state solve cost 40..10000 nodes; target 5 roots/ply; 29 roots qualified
allis_a1_a3.interpretation: The three cheapest Allis rule families have high partial coverage in nontrivial mid/late residual states and can sometimes form complete conservative hold certificates. No false hold was observed. Full-cover frequency is modest, supporting them as strong certificate primitives rather than a standalone complete evaluator.
